base.description: CRS520-4XS-16XQ-RM - sixteen 100G QSFP28 cages, four 25G SFP28 cages, two 10G Ethernet ports and an RJ45 console, with two hot-swap AC supplies and four hot-swap fans (part of the chassis in this model). The box holds two power cords, rack ears, rear support ears, a cable management bracket and a fastening set.

description: MikroTik CRS520-4XS-16XQ-RM is a fixed 1U Cloud Router Switch, 443 mm wide with rack ears in the box, with sixteen 100 Gigabit QSFP28 cages and four 25 Gigabit SFP28 cages, two 10 Gigabit Ethernet ports printed MGMT / BOOT and an RJ45 serial console, and runs RouterOS v7. The front carries the sixteen QSFP28 cages in eight stacked pairs with four lamps each, the four SFP28 cages in two stacked pairs, the console, RESET, four status lamps, the two Ethernet ports and a vent strip along each edge. The rear carries two hot-swap AC supply modules with their C14 inlets and four hot-swap fan modules. The brochure prints no part number for the supplies or the fans, so they are part of the chassis and there are no bays.

gaps.note: The brochure's powering table prints a nominal current of 10.25 A and a maximum of 12.5 A, and the photograph prints "100-240 V ~2,5 A MAX, 50/60Hz" between the supplies; the two are not reconciled by any held document (the brochure's pair may be the 12 V side). The brochure's 150 W maximum is followed in parentheses by 220 W with both supplies; 150 W is carried as the maximum and the 220 W is kept in the text of `power-input`. The legend is drawn as printed.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's statement of what the currents and the 220 W mean.

gaps.note: The brochure calls the two power supplies hot-swap and prints no part number; no data sheet or drawing of the supply is held, and no document says what covers an empty slot. They are drawn as part of the chassis with their inlets and no bay is added; the base configuration exports two AC power ports.
gaps.wanted: The supply's part number and a statement of what a slot holds when empty.

gaps.note: The brochure calls the four fans hot-swap and prints no part number; the photograph shows four numbered modules. They are drawn as fan guards in the chassis, with no bay, and no fan redundancy is written.
gaps.wanted: The fan module's part number and MikroTik's redundancy statement.

gaps.note: The brochure says the switch can also be powered by the PW48V-12V150W hot-swap -48 V DC telecom supply, available separately. No held document draws it or gives its size, so no module is added and no bay offers it.
gaps.wanted: A data sheet or drawing of the PW48V-12V150W.

gaps.note: Searched the brochure, the page and the safety book for an LED table: none. The four lamps of each QSFP28 cage, the two of each SFP28 cage and the USER, POWER 2, POWER 1 and FAULT lamps carry the component's own vocabulary and no meaning is stated. The lamps' resting colour comes from the lamp component and is not changed here: the photographs show the lamps unlit grey and the render draws them with the component's own colour.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's LED description for the CRS520-4XS-16XQ-RM.

gaps.note: Photograph 2354 shows the lamps as mid brown-grey to pink-beige ovals and the two management link lamps olive green and yellow; the brochure's picture of the same face draws them black. The lamps are the lamp component's own resting colour, #3a3938, and no lit lamp is drawn; both readings are recorded here and neither is chosen.
gaps.wanted: A statement of which picture shows the lamps as they ship.

gaps.note: The QSFP28 and SFP28 cages, the management jacks and the C14 inlets are shared parts drawn for other boxes. Against photograph 2354 their frames are black with a thin copper-beige rim and a bright silver tab where the shared parts draw near-black blocks, a light blue-grey frame and one shared frame for the two management jacks. The drawn parts are not changed here, because a new version of a shared part is a follow-up that moves other boxes' drawings.
gaps.wanted: A new version of each shared part drawn to these cages and jacks.

gaps.note: The rear's handles are chrome loops and its thumbscrews knurled in photograph 2353; the medians sampled from them are dark because chrome reflects the bronze modules, so they are drawn as flat bars and pills in those medians. The face between the modules reads #e9e9e8 where lit and #bbbbb7 in shade in 2353, neutral, while the front face reads #e0dcd5 in 2354; the chassis has one colour, #e0dcd5, from the front. The fan screws and the small hole at the upper left of each fan are drawn estimated from 2353, at about 1 mm.
gaps.wanted: A straight-on, evenly lit rear photograph.

gaps.note: Photograph 2352 reads the right wall about #d9d6d3 to #dcdad6, slightly darker and greyer than the front's #e0dcd5, which is shading on a wall that faces away from the light. The wall is drawn in the chassis colour. The 37 hexagonal holes in rows of 7 and 8, the lid seam, the three lid screws and the step at the front corner are drawn from that photograph, the screws estimated to about 3 mm along the wall.
gaps.wanted: A straight-on photograph of the right wall.

gaps.note: The sixteen QSFP28 cages are two rows, the upper row turned half a turn from the lower as the other stacked cages are. Photograph 2354 and the brochure's close view show each cage as a dark window with a light rim and, in the lower row, a ledge at the bottom of the window; they do not show which side holds the contacts or the latch tongue clearly enough to read, so the turn is carried as drawn and not confirmed. The SFP28 cages, whose pull tabs face each other across the rows, and the RJ45 jacks, whose key notches and lamps are readable, do match the photograph.
gaps.wanted: A straight-on, close photograph of a QSFP28 cage in each row.

gaps.note: The brochure's included parts and COVERAGE name the optional 23-40 Rack Rail R0 (brochure 3-40_RACK_RAIL_R0_260621.pdf, named for the CRS520, CRS804, CRS812, CCR2216 and RDS2216). The kit is not modelled here: the later CRS8xx batch adds it for all five, and the CRS520 will list it when that batch adds it. No `kind: kit` contract and no `chassis.kits` entry is written.

The brochure lists "Rackmount rear support ears" and a "Cable managment bracket" among the included parts. The ear model has only front ears, so none is drawn, and the bracket is not drawn either; no held document dimensions either part.
gaps.wanted: A drawing of the rear support ears and the bracket.

gaps.note: No held document shows the left wall: the drawing has no wall view and the photographs show the right wall, the front and the rear. It is left empty and is not drawn from the right.
The drawing's top plan shows a plain lid and no vent; the photographs show a plain lid with vent slots only along the front edge, which the front face carries. No document shows the underside.
Neither the brochure nor the page gives a weight.
The saved product page carries no Discontinued badge and MikroTik publishes no end-of-life page, so no lifecycle is written.

brackets.note: Photograph 2354 and the brochure's close view print a thin bracket line over each port group, hooked down at both ends: over the 100G QSFP28 cages from 7.6 to 198.1 mm and over the 25G SFP28 cages from 205.5 to 240.4 mm, 6.3 mm down, the hooks 3.8 mm long in the photograph (4 times enlargement at 5.33 px per mm), drawn 3.0 and 2.0 mm long so that they stop above the lamps, and two hooks over and under the left lamp column running right to USER and FAULT. They are stroked paths 0.2 mm wide. Port numerals are printed over each cage: QSFP28 1 to 16, SFP28 1 to 4.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: The brochure says "two hot-swap power supplies and four hot-swap fans". Photograph 2353 shows two supply modules, each with a C14 inlet, a steel handle and a vent, and four fan modules numbered 1 to 4, each with a handle and a round fan guard. No held document prints a part number for the supply or the fan (the brochure, the page and the safety book were searched), so none is named: they are part of the chassis, as on juniper/ex2300-24t, and there are no bays (gaps `hot-swap-supplies` and `hot-swap-fans`). No document says what covers an empty slot. The brochure's optional PW48V-12V150W is not the supply that ships and no document draws it (gap `optional-dc-supply`). The legend between the supplies and the fans reads "POWER 1 / POWER 2" and "100-240 V ~2,5 A MAX, 50/60Hz".

chassis.note: 443 x 367 x 44, as the drawing prints them; the brochure prints 443 x 367 x 44 and agrees. The drawing also dimensions 19.1 mm beyond the rear (the fan and supply handles) that is not part of the 367.

datasheet.note: The brochure is MikroTik's datasheet for the model: product code CRS520-4XS-16XQ-RM, quad-core AL52400 2 GHz ARM 64 bit, 4 GB DDR4 RAM, 128 MB NAND, 2 x 1G/2.5G/5G/10G Ethernet (10M, 100M, 1G and 10G speeds), 4 x 25G SFP28, 16 x 100G QSFP28, switch chip 98CX8410, 443 x 367 x 44 mm, RouterOS v7 only, level 5, -20 to +50 C. Powering: two AC inputs, 100-240 V, 47-63 Hz, nominal current 10.25 A, maximum current 12.5 A, 123 W maximum without attachments, 150 W maximum (220 W with both supplies). Included parts: 2 power cords, rack ears, rear support ears, a cable management bracket, a fastening set. The text says "two hot-swap power supplies and four hot-swap fans" and states no redundancy form. It also names the PW48V-12V150W hot-swap -48 V DC telecom supply, available separately. Each figure is filed as the document words it.

ears.note: Rack ears are in the box (the brochure and the page: Rackmount ears) and the drawing's front view draws them at both ends. They are shipped flush with the face and are not drawn on it; no `at` is written. The rear support ears, the cable management bracket and the optional rail are not drawn (gaps `rear-support-ears`, `rack-rail-kit`).

front-layout.note: From the drawing's front view. Sixteen QSFP28 frames 22 mm wide and 12.3 mm tall in two rows of eight, frame centres 18.6 mm from the left and a 24.07 mm pitch, the upper row centred 18.1 mm down and the lower 31.6 mm; four round lamps 4.0 mm apart over the upper row and under the lower row of each pair. Four SFP28 frames 15.6 mm wide and 12 mm tall in two columns at 212.9 and 232.2 mm and two rows centred 18.1 and 31.5 mm down, with two round lamps over the upper row and under the lower row. The console jack plate is 17.8 x 14.3 mm at 247.4 mm, 9.4 mm, over a 33.8 x 15.1 mm plate at 247.4 mm, 25.6 mm, holding the two Ethernet jacks. RESET is a ring at 271.4 mm, 19.1 mm. Four round lamps sit in two rows at 279.6 and 284.0 mm and 13.3 and 17.8 mm. Rows of vent slots run along the top and bottom edges.

gate-1.note: The drawing's front view body is 1159.5 px wide between its end lines for the printed 443 mm (2.617 px per mm in the page image) and 44.5 mm tall, the printed 44. At that scale a pixel is 0.4 mm, so every x and y below is taken from the body's top-left corner of the front view to about 0.5 mm. The rear and the right wall are read off photographs scaled from the 443 mm width.

lamps.note: Photograph 2354 prints USER, POWER 2, POWER 1 and FAULT beside the four lamps. USER and FAULT have brackets that end at the left column, over and under it, so the left column is USER (upper) and FAULT (lower); POWER 2 and POWER 1 are on the rows of the right column. Each cage has the lamps the drawing draws, four for a QSFP28 and two for an SFP28; no document says what a lamp shows (gap `led-states`).

management-and-console.note: Photograph 2354 prints CONSOLE over the upper jack and 10G MGMT / BOOT between the numbers 1 and 2 under the two lower jacks. The brochure counts two 1G/2.5G/5G/10G Ethernet ports supporting 10M, 100M, 1G and 10G speeds; they are filed at 10g, the highest, as the CRS312 files its 10G jacks.

port-numbering.note: The metal prints 2 4 6 8 10 12 14 16 over the QSFP28 stacks and 1 3 5 7 9 11 13 15 under them, 2 and 4 over the SFP28 cages and 1 and 3 under them, so the lower cage of a stack takes the odd number. The groups are printed 100G QSFP28 and 25G SFP28, and 1 and 2 under the Ethernet ports (photograph 2354).

rear-layout.note: From photograph 2353 (the rear, from slightly above), x across the 443 mm at 4.0 px per mm and y estimated (the photograph looks down, 3.8 px per mm). Two supply modules about 63 mm wide at 2.5 and 65.9 mm with their inlets centred 54.0 and 117.4 mm and 22.5 mm down; four fan modules 60.4 mm wide at 158.5, 227.6, 296.2 and 364.0 mm. Read to about 2 mm, as seen from behind. Measured again on the photograph at 5.36 px per mm (the face's 2360 px for 443 mm): each fan's honeycomb ring is 204 px, 38.0 mm across the hole tips (drawn 37.5, estimated), centred 37.4 mm from its module's left edge, so right of the handle and not in the middle of the plate, round a solid hub 20.0 mm across (107 px); the guard's holes are 25 x 21.5 px, 4.7 mm across the corners and 4.0 across the flats, in columns 23.3 px (4.37 mm) apart and rows 24.9 px (4.67 mm), nine columns across the ring. The renderer's honeycomb tile is 8.86 x 5.11 mm with holes 5.1 mm across the corners: the tile is scaled by 0.914 on both axes to 8.1 x 4.67 mm, which draws the hole as read and the rows as read and the columns 7 per cent closer than read (4.05 mm against 4.37); a regular hexagon cannot be both. The tile's phase puts a hole on each ring's centre. The supply vents' holes are larger, 29 x 24 px, 5.4 mm across the corners, columns 28.2 px (5.27 mm) and rows 29.9 px (5.6 mm, not corrected for the look from above): the tile is scaled by 1.06 to 9.39 x 5.42 mm, with a hole at 10.6 mm and 10.3 mm down in the first supply and 63.4 mm further in the second; the field is the honeycomb's extent left of the handle, 27.0 x 28.4 mm. The earlier fields drew the base tile and a 36 mm guard in the middle of the plate. The photograph shows no honeycomb under the hub. Each fan module has a chrome handle 4.6 mm wide and 38 mm tall 12.8 mm from the module's left edge and a knurled thumbscrew 7.2 x 13.4 mm left of it (photograph 2353 at 5.4 px per mm, x from the face's left edge at 150 px, y at 0.88 of that); each supply has a handle 4.0 x 39.8 mm, two latch tabs above and below the inlet and a thumbscrew at its left edge. Five chassis screws 4.4 mm across (133.1, 224.8, 294.0, 363.1 and 438.3 mm) sit between the modules and at the right end. The legend POWER 1 / POWER 2 is underlined 25.8 mm and each fan numeral is followed by a filled arrowhead (estimated, about 2 mm). Each inlet is turned so that its earth pin is at the right as seen from behind: photograph 2353 (5.36 px per mm) shows the first inlet's housing 139 x 159 px (25.9 x 29.7 mm, pixel box 361,709 to 500,868) with its two line pins aligned at the left and the offset middle pin at the right (estimated, about 1 mm); the first drawing had the earth pin at the left.

side-layout.note: Photograph 2352 shows a field of 37 small hexagonal perforations on the right wall, near the front, in staggered rows of 7 and 8 (five rows). The wall's four corners in the photograph (a perspective transform of the quad onto 367 x 44 mm, 5 px per mm) put the field about 35 x 17 mm, 11 mm from the front and 14 mm down, good to about 3 mm; it is drawn as two `motif` fields of one hexagon, 2.43 x 2.8 mm, on a 4.55 x 6.8 mm pitch, the rows of 8 and the rows of 7 offset by half a column (estimated, hexagon size and pitch read off the unwarped photograph). The lid seam and its step at the front corner are drawn as one printed line, and three crosshead screws sit on the lid flange. The same unwarp (5.45 px per mm, good to about 1 mm along the wall) shows four small round holes 2.2 mm across, drawn as screw holes: two beside the field at 61.8 mm from the front, 14.8 and 29.3 mm down, and two near the rear at 314.5 and 342.0 mm, 19.9 and 19.5 mm down; each fill is the median of its own dark pixels (about 70 to 107 pixels each, spreads 15 to 27), estimated. No held document shows the left wall. The drawing has no wall view.

vents.note: The front's top strip is two rows of rectangular slots (photograph 2354, the drawing's front view and the brochure's close view), drawn as `motif` tiles because the slots are square-cut 4.0 mm rectangles with a corner radius of about 0.15 mm, which `slots-h` (rounded ends) does not draw. Read off photograph 2354 at 5.33 px per mm (the face's 2365 px at y 700 for 443 mm; the photograph looks down, the face reads 0.93 of that vertically): the slot pitch is 27.15 px (17 pitches, 461.5 px), 5.09 mm, and every slot is the same width, 21.7 px, 4.07 mm. Measured on the photograph at 4 times enlargement the slots are 1.5 mm tall (6 to 7.5 px) and the rows 3.0 mm apart (14.75 px): row 1 at 0.9 mm, row 2 at 3.9 mm, each its own motif field with a tile 5.09 x 1.5 mm (the first reading, 2.0 mm slots 3.5 mm apart, took the drawing's 14.4 px over two rows). The second row has no slots where the photograph prints the legends 100G QSFP28 and 25G SFP28, so it is three fields that stop and start on whole slot pitches: 4.1 to 95.72, 110.99 to 212.79 and 233.15 to 438.1 mm. The bottom edge is not a row of slots but 54 shallow light notches, 4.0 x 1.5 mm on the same pitch (photograph 2354, 4 times enlargement: 8 px deep, light grey inside, #d3cac3 over three boxes of 70 to 85 pixels), drawn as plain rects so that they are light. The strips start 4.1 mm from the left and run 434.0 mm, and the notches 278.0 mm, the drawing's extents (the photograph puts the first slot 3.0 mm in; the drawing's body edge is a double line). The rear fields are hexagon honeycombs as the photograph shows: see `rear-layout`.
